title: VIRTUAL: Vector-based Dynamic Power Estimation via Decoupled Multi-Modality Learning
problem: Dynamic power analysis requires gate-level synthesis and simulation, creating critical bottleneck in iterative design flows; estimating power directly from RTL is challenging without manual feature engineering.
motivation: Faster power estimation enables rapid design iteration and optimization.
method: Multi-modality learning framework with decoupled feature extraction: transformer encoder extracts temporal patterns from input port waveforms, GNN captures structural dependencies from RTL; self-supervised contrastive learning across modalities, lightweight fusion module for embeddings, power prediction head for fixed clock period estimation.
key_novelty: Decoupled multi-modality learning combining waveform temporal patterns and RTL structural features for power estimation.
contributions: Transformer-based encoder for waveform temporal pattern extraction
Graph neural network for RTL structural dependency modeling
Self-supervised contrastive learning across sequential and graph modalities
limitations: 23.43% MAPE is moderate; requires labeled gate-level data for training; generalization to unseen RTL designs unclear.
